The '''2022 Exeter City Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022 to elect members to [[Exeter City Council]] in [[Devon]], England. This was the same day as other [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|local elections]] in the United Kingdom. 17 of the 39 seats were up for election, one councillor in each of the 13 wards, and 4 by-elections. These wards were last contested in [[2018 Exeter City Council election|2018]].

==Council composition==
The Labour Party have a majority of 17 on the council.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Find your councillor – Current council information – Exeter City Council|url=https://exeter.gov.uk/council-and-democracy/councillors-and-meetings/find-your-councillor/current-council-information/|access-date=2022-02-14|website=Exeter City Council website|language=en-GB}}</ref> The Conservatives are the main opposition with 6 councillors.<ref name=":0" /> The Liberal Democrat, Green and Independent Councillors formed a "Progressive Group" following the [[2019 Exeter City Council election|2019 elections]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Clark|first=Daniel|date=2019-05-13|title=New Progressive Group formed to 'challenge Exeter's one party state'|url=https://www.devonlive.com/news/devon-news/new-progressive-group-formed-challenge-2855975|access-date=2022-02-14|website=DevonLive|language=en}}</ref>

In these elections, 10 wards up for election currently have a Labour councillor (Alphington; Exwick; Heavitree; Mincinglake & Whipton; Newtown & St Leonards; Pennsylvania; Pinhoe; Priory; St Davids; and St Thomas), 2 have Conservative councillors (St Loyes; and Topsham) and 1 has a Liberal Democrat councillor (Duryard and St James). 

In addition to these seats, four by-elections have so far been announced in the Exwick, Heavitree, Pennsylvania and Priory wards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Election Notices - Exeter City Council |url=https://exeter.gov.uk/council-and-democracy/elections-and-voting/2022-city-elections/election-notices/ |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=Exeter City Council website |language=en-GB}}</ref> In order to retain their overall majority on the councillor, Labour need to win at least six seats.

== Outgoing Councillors ==
Each ward has the following outgoing councillor:

=== Alphington ===

* Cllr. Bob Foale (Labour): Portfolio Holder for Transformation & Environment;<ref name=":0" /> First elected in [[2016 Exeter City Council election|2016]].

=== Duryard and St James ===

* Cllr. Kevin Mitchell (Liberal Democrat): Liberal Democrat group leader; Progressive Group leader;<ref name=":0" /> First elected in [[2003 Exeter City Council election|2003]].

=== Exwick ===

* Cllr. Rachel Sutton (Labour): Portfolio Holder for Net Zero Exeter 2030;<ref name=":0" /> First elected in [[2010 Exeter City Council election|2010]].
* A by-election will be held due to the resignation of Cllr. Ollie Pearson.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2022-03-23 |title=Your Councillors |url=http://committees.exeter.gov.uk/mgMemberIndex.aspx?FN=WARD&VW=LIST&PIC=0 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=committees.exeter.gov.uk |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Heavitree ===

* Cllr. Greg Sheldon (Labour);<ref name=":0" /> First elected in 1996.
* A by-election will be held due to the resignation of Cllr. Chris Buswell.<ref name=":1" />

=== Mincinglake and Whipton ===

* Cllr. Naima Allcock (Labour);<ref name=":0" /> First elected in [[2021 Exeter City Council election|2021]].

=== Newtown and St Leonards ===

* Cllr. Matthew Vizard (Labour);<ref name=":0" /> First elected in 2017.

=== Pennsylvania ===

* Cllr. Jane Begley (Labour);<ref name=":0" /> First elected in [[2018 Exeter City Council election|2018]].
* A by-election will be held due to the death of Cllr. Ian Quance.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Merritt |first=Anita |date=2022-03-23 |title=Exeter's deputy lord mayor has died |url=https://www.devonlive.com/news/devon-news/exeters-deputy-lord-mayor-died-6849701 |access-date=2022-03-24 |website=DevonLive |language=en}}</ref>

=== Pinhoe ===

* Cllr. Duncan Wood (Labour);<ref name=":0" /> First elected in [[2016 Exeter City Council election|2016]].

=== Priory ===

* Cllr. Tony Wardle (Labour);<ref name=":0" /> First elected in [[2008 Exeter City Council election|2008]].
* A by-election will be held due to the resignation of Cllr. Alys Martin.<ref name=":1" />

=== St Davids ===

* Cllr. Luke Sills (Labour);<ref name=":0" /> First elected in [[2016 Exeter City Council election|2016]].

=== St Loyes ===

* Cllr. Peter Holland (Conservative);<ref name=":0" /> First elected in [[2014 Exeter City Council election|2014]].

=== St Thomas ===

* Cllr. Laura Wright (Labour): Deputy Leader and Portfolio Holder for Council Housing Development and Services;<ref name=":0" /> First elected in [[2018 Exeter City Council election|2018]].

=== Topsham ===

* Cllr. Keith Sparkes (Conservative);<ref name=":0" /> First elected in 2019.
